title: Tenant throttle sleuth journal and minimal runbook
content:
Summary:

This doc is an on-call field journal for a late-afternoon degradation in a dedicated GPU pool (eu-west-2). Symptoms: sustained p99 latency rise for generation endpoints, sudden 30% drop in effective throughput for 45 minutes, and a cascade of eviction alerts. Multiple tenants experienced degraded tail latency; one high-volume tenant (tenant-corp-42) was the suspected amplifier.

Why this exists: informal capture of timeline, quick hypotheses, temporary mitigations applied during the event, and a minimal runbook sketch to reduce time-to-first-mitigation on similar incidents. This is intentionally terse and pragmatic — preserve facts, decisions, and follow-ups.

Incident timeline (UTC):
- 2025-11-02 15:08: alert: autoscaler evictions spike (alert id: SRE-EV-3301)
- 2025-11-02 15:09: paging oncall (rotation: Samira)
- 2025-11-02 15:12: verified p99 growth from 80ms -> 420ms on /v1/complete (generation) across pool gw-eu-w2-poolB
- 2025-11-02 15:17: throughput measured: per-pool tokens/s dropped 28% vs baseline
- 2025-11-02 15:22: noisy-tenant hypothesis: tenant-corp-42 spike in long-context streaming sessions (seen in trace ids)
- 2025-11-02 15:30: containment: set tenant-corp-42 to limited concurrency profile (manual override) via edge-routes
- 2025-11-02 15:41: one GPU node (g4-58) showed sustained kernel preemption warnings; drained and reprovisioned
- 2025-11-02 15:55: autoscaler config rollback: revert recent increase of eviction aggressiveness (PR link in linked_artifacts)
- 2025-11-02 16:12: latency trending back to baseline; throughput recovered by 90% of pre-incident
- 2025-11-02 16:45: incident declared mitigated; monitoring on extended watch until 2025-11-03 03:00

Immediate evidence collected:
- kube events dump for pool nodes (attached to Linear SRE-4827)
- trace samples showing large KV-cache warmups from tenant-corp-42 (high prefix miss rate)
- per-tenant concurrency spikes from ingress logs (tenant header + rate)
- node-level GPU telemetry: elevated SM utilization and periodic driver RT warnings

Initial hypotheses (ordered by plausibility at the time):
1) Noisy tenant amplification + KV cache amplification: tenant-corp-42 opened many long-context sessions that missed cached prefixes, causing disproportionate token compute and KV cache pressure, increasing per-token latency and triggering autoscaler eviction signals.
2) Autoscaler hysteresis misconfiguration: eviction thresholds were tuned aggressively for burst smoothing; when kernel preemption warnings appeared, the autoscaler over-evicted leading to capacity oscillation.
3) Underlying driver/firmware transient: one node showed interrupts and required reprovision; could be separate but amplified the pool-level instability.

Actions taken (chronological with rationale):
- Quick containment: throttle tenant-corp-42 concurrency at the edge (15:30). Rationale: reduce immediate KV/cache pressure and token compute load while we triage. This lowered pool-wide p99 within 8–10 minutes.
- Drain and reprovision node g4-58 (15:41). Rationale: clear suspected driver/firmware flakiness; node returned healthy with reduced warnings.
- Rollback autoscaler eviction aggressiveness (15:55). Rationale: prevent cascade of evictions that amplify tail latency.
- Set synthetic canary traffic and extended watch (16:00). Rationale: ensure steady behaviour over multiple traffic patterns before fully relaxing mitigations.

What worked:
- Tenant-level quick throttle (edge override) produced the fastest observable improvement in pool p99 (effect seen ~8–10 min).
- Having the node reprovision path automated allowed a reproducible remediation during oncall.

What didn't work / open concerns:
- Detection lag: initial alerts were autoscaler-eviction-centric; we should have a multi-signal alert that correlates per-tenant concurrency spikes + KV miss amplification to reduce time-to-first-action.
- No quick rollback for tenant routing policies in the console; we used a CLI edge command that is not ergonomic for oncall.
- The autoscaler config PR had passed staging tests but lacked a ramped rollout; need rollout gating for config changes that affect eviction thresholds.

Minimal runbook sketch (for SRE runbook doc inclusion) — "Dedicated pool noisy-tenant event":
1) Detection:
   - Primary signals: p99 generation latency > 2x baseline for 5m across pool OR pool eviction-rate > 5/min for 3m.
   - Secondary signals: per-tenant concurrency > 95th baseline for 10m, KV prefix miss rate spike > 2x
2) Initial triage (first 10 min):
   - Check pool dashboard: identify which pools/nodes report eviction spikes and p99 regressions.
   - Query ingress logs for top 5 tenants by requests in the last 15m.
   - If single tenant accounts for >40% of requests and shows long-context or streaming sessions, flag as candidate noisy tenant.
3) Containment (first 20 min):
   - Apply edge concurrency cap for candidate tenant(s) (CLI: edgectl route update --tenant <id> --max-concurrency 8) — choose conservative cap that reduces KV churn.
   - If node-level telemetry shows driver warnings, cordon + drain suspect node(s) and reprovision.
4) Stabilize (20–60 min):
   - Revert any autoscaler config changes recently rolled out; set autoscaler to conservative eviction settings.
   - Run synthetic load to validate p99 and throughput stability.
5) Recovery and post-incident (after stable 2h):
   - Remove temporary tenant throttles gradually; monitor for re-emergence.
   - Open postmortem ticket with timeline, artifacts, root cause analysis, and remediation plan.

Playbook commands (examples for oncall):
- Check top tenants: curl -s "https://metrics/api/top-tenants?pool=gw-eu-w2-poolB&window=15m" | jq
- Throttle tenant: edgectl route update --tenant tenant-corp-42 --max-concurrency 8 --reason "sre: temporary throttle during noisy-tenant event"
- Reprovision node: infractl reprovision --node g4-58 --pool gw-eu-w2-poolB
- Rollback autoscaler config: git checkout origin/staging -- deploy/autoscaler/eviction.yaml && infractl apply -f deploy/autoscaler/eviction.yaml

Follow-ups & owners (short list):
- SRE-4827 (Samira) — full postmortem and diagram of cache amplification path
- PLAT-1182 (Javier) — console UX for tenant throttle rollback + one-click guardrails
- INFR-772 (Mei) — autoscaler rollout policy: require canary traffic or config gate for eviction thresholds
- ENG-mlops-331 (Liam) — investigate model-serving behaviour for long-context KV cache miss patterns

Notes for the postmortem:
- Collect full hitchhiking traces for tenant-corp-42 sessions (correlate trace ids with ingress headers).
- Snapshot autoscaler metrics and alarm history for the 2 hours surrounding the event.
- Evaluate whether the autoscaler change that increased eviction aggressiveness was rolled to this pool without a percentage rollout; if so, require staged configuration rollouts and monitor signal binding (p99 + per-tenant concurrency) before full rollouts.

Open questions (to resolve in postmortem):
- Was tenant-corp-42 spike organic or due to a customer rollout (feature toggle) we didn't see? Reach out to AE owner.
- Can we add a short-circuit to autoscaler logic: if per-tenant concurrency spike detected, prefer soft-throttle over immediate eviction?
- Should we introduce KV cache reservation for high-SLA tenants to reduce amplification risk?

Appendix: quick artifacts references
- Alerts: SRE-EV-3301 (eviction spike), SRE-LAT-5402 (p99 grow)
- Tickets: Linear SRE-4827
- PRs/Config: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2148 (autoscaler eviction tweak rollback)

End of journal. This doc should be moved into the canonical runbook folder after the postmortem completes and owners sign off. Keep as working notes until then.
